venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Baugh ran for 160 and three scores. Faulkner would not let FAU play him one way. Coleman and Johnson got the ball back. The short throw stayed open for ninety plays.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — compressed, no yardage nicknames. Fan rail stays empty until Charles approves.
headline: Baugh ran through them. Faulkner kept changing the look. The short throw stayed free.

offense.body:
You cannot put a card on this offense. That is the point.

Faulkner does not install a system you can memorize. He asks a new question before you finish the last one. Same start. Different answer. Backside still live.

Creep up for Baugh and he throws the short one to Brown. First man misses. Brown scores from 49 yards. Long touchdown, short throw.

Follow the tackles who look like they are leading a run and the ball goes the other way — Brown, three linemen already out in front. Later Clark. Same picture. On his touchdown those big people are already down the field.

Stay put and play Baugh and he runs it. Scores from 12 with those linemen actually leading him. Third quarter, everybody knows, and he still rips off 61 yards.

He keeps changing the picture. Baugh is most of it.

Receivers way out wide. Brown and Wilson one behind the other. Extra men on Baugh, and someone is alone with half the field. Not a trick. Just room.

More players on one side. A man in motion. FAU still counting when it snaps. Not decoration. Numbers.

The fake run is the lie and the truth. Sometimes the tackles leave and the ball follows the three in the middle. Sometimes those tackles really are leading Baugh and he walks into it. When they need one yard, nobody leaves — sneak, Philo from the 3.

They will pull a tackle on a pass too. The rusher has to choose: chase Philo or honor the fake. Either way he is late. They showed it more than they cashed it. They will hand it off from that same look.

Philo with Baugh behind him showed up once — run, then Wilson sitting in the grass for 19 yards. One look. Not the offense. Wilson moved the chains because he sits where you leave him.

Philo ran the offense. In and out. Eyes down when rushed. Step up, still find somebody. He does not have to be the hero. Stockton walked in from the 11 on a ball that was a little late. FAU finally crowded Baugh, the line looked like pass, Abrams over the top for 63 yards. The pick is Mays — ball off his hands, Sweeney sitting. When Philo holds it, the play dies.

Baugh is the night. Fourteen carries, 160 yards, three rushing scores. FAU filled every hole on some plays and he still ripped it. That is not scheme. That is the best player in the building. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting eleven on him. Clark is the change of pace. They will not run Baugh thirty times.

The line is clean — almost no penalties, no late-shift disaster like last year. They are not getting out to the linebackers fast. The wide run is not ready. Faulkner still shows it so you have to honor the outside. His move: do not ask this line to block everybody. Leave people unblocked on purpose.

The snaps over Philo’s head are Moore’s hands. Sumrall already said it. The one that lost twenty yards inside the five is the kind that loses real games. Philo ran it himself once, FAU’s end still there, lost two yards. Idea fine. Play lost.

They block down the field like they mean it. Ten becomes thirty. Micah Jones blows up one man, then the next, and they throw him the last touchdown. Same idea as Clark — big person in front of a skill player.

A coordinator who flexes to what you are weak at. A back you cannot tackle if they do not put extra men on him. A quarterback who ran the offense. Clean the snap, the play Philo ran and lost, and the ball off Mays. The rest is a headache.
bullets: You creep up for Baugh, he throws the short one to Brown. Brown scores from 49.
You follow the fake, the ball goes the other way — Brown, later Clark.
You stay put, Baugh runs it — including 61 yards when everybody knew.
Clean the snap, the play Philo ran and lost, and the ball off Mays.

defense.body:
FAU wants the short throw until you take it away. Florida never took it away.

Corners lined up yards off. Linebackers not standing where that short ball lands. You show them something before the snap and give them the same throw after it. Ninety plays. Ten of thirteen on third down. Henry and Valsin lived on the five-to-eight yard catch. Sumrall said it: third-and-1, you cannot have your corner nine yards off. That happened. That is the tax.

White will live with the short throw if they tackle. They did not tackle enough of it, and nobody stood where the ball lands, so FAU kept moving the chains.

He still has a real idea. He moves people. Woods is how he does it. On third down he shifts him. Sometimes Woods is rushing from the outside. Sometimes he walks inside and someone else has that outside rush. The tackle never knows who is coming. Mix it. Often.

When Veltkamp holds it, the idea pays. Coleman acts like the middle is open, the ball goes outside, Coleman is already there. That pick is bait. Not a blitz. He moved the quarterback’s eyes. He tips the next one. Johnson goes up and gets it. Same idea. Bett beats the quarterback at the 1, ball out, Johnson falls on it. McCloud wins fourth-and-2. The rush finally finishes.

Safeties were clean — Coleman, Thornton. Clark played a real night in the slot and lost one ball to the corner of the end zone with no help. That throw is the cost of lining up yards off. Valsin scored from 20. Same play Stockton ran the other way.

What leaked is the stuff inside the plan. The pile at the 1 — they had enough people, they lost the yard. The man on the outside left and Veltkamp walked in from 7. Woods has to stay there. When he chases, FAU runs at him.

Later they sent four rushers and still played the corners off. That kills the deep ball. It also leaves the short throw and the throw to the corner alive.

They were ready for how fast FAU plays. They were not staring at the sideline when it snapped. Veltkamp is a real quarterback — he can throw it and run it. Sumrall called the defense atrocious at times because ninety plays and those fourth downs are what you get when the short throw is free.

Stand where the short ball lands. Keep Woods on the outside when the quarterback runs it. Mix Woods. Make him hold it. Coleman already showed you what that looks like.
bullets: The short throw was open. That is why FAU ran 90 plays.
White moves Woods so the tackle never knows who is coming.
When Veltkamp holds it, Coleman and Johnson take it.
Fix the pile at the 1, the man on the outside, and the throw to the corner.

specials.body: Durkin from 53. Clean. Florida never punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt starts Florida’s second score.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt starts Florida’s second score.

keys: Baugh was the night. Faulkner kept changing the look around him.
Philo ran the offense. Clean the snap, the play he ran and lost, and the ball off Mays.
Coleman, Johnson, Bett showed up. The short throw stayed open. Ninety plays.
Fix the pile at the 1, the man on the outside, and the throw to the corner.

nextWeek.look: They will throw it short and the quarterback will run it. Sixkiller is their guy. Florida will still hand it to Baugh and keep changing the picture. White has to stand on that short throw and keep Woods on the outside when Sixkiller runs it himself.
